newEntriesNeeded.title: undefined() function for global variable existence check
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use undefined() to check if a global variable has been assigned before accessing it.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: undefined(!!globalVar) returns TRUE if the global is unassigned, FALSE if assigned.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_addErrorToList
if(undefined(!!ramCommonLogger)) then
  !!ramCommonLogger = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Accessing unassigned global without check
!!ramCommonLogger.addLogDetails(...) -- may crash if not initialized
pitfalls: Only works with global variables (!!), not local variables (!)

newEntriesNeeded.title: STRING.unset() method for existence check
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use unset() on STRING or ARRAY to check if the variable has been assigned a value.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: unset() returns TRUE if the variable is unassigned/undefined, FALSE if it holds a value.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
!str.unset() -- TRUE if !str is not set
!arr.unset() -- TRUE if !arr is not set
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_loadReportDetails
if(!viewDetails.set() AND !viewDetails.size().eq(7)) then
  -- process details
else
  !this.clearData()
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Checking set() vs unset() confusion
if(!str.unset()) then -- wrong: checks if unset, but code expects set
  ...
pitfalls: set() and unset() are inverses: !x.set() is equivalent to !x.unset().not()

newEntriesNeeded.title: OBJECT.objecttype() method for runtime type identification
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use objecttype() on any PML2 object to get its type name as a STRING at runtime.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: objecttype() returns a STRING containing the object type identifier.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax: !this.objecttype() -- returns the type name of the current object
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Hardcoding type names instead of using objecttype()
!!ramCommonLogger.addLogDetails('JACEISDELIVERYMANAGER', !errorList)
pitfalls: Returns the declared type name, not the variable name

newEntriesNeeded.title: BLOCK evaluate with !evalIndex special variable
newEntriesNeeded.principle: When evaluating a BLOCK on an ARRAY, !evalIndex is a special variable available inside the block that holds the current index.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: !columns.evaluate(object BLOCK(|!columns[!evalIndex].string()|)) iterates over !columns, with !evalIndex set to each index.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_columnCollection
!columnRefNos = !columns.evaluate(object BLOCK(|!columns[!evalIndex].string()|))
-- CB obj_09_loadReport
!headings = !headings.evaluate(object BLOCK(|!headings[!evalIndex][1]|))
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using a regular loop instead of evaluate
DO !i FROM 1 TO !columns.Size()
  !result.Append(!columns[!i].string())
ENDDO
pitfalls: !evalIndex is only available inside the BLOCK expression, not outside
BLOCK evaluates each element; the result is an ARRAY of the evaluated values

newEntriesNeeded.title: PROJECT CODE system variable with !!evar()
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PROJECT CODE is a PML1 system query variable that returns the current PDMS project code. Use !!evar() to evaluate it in PML2 context.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: !!evar(|PDMSUSER|) returns the PDMS user data path. !!evar(!varName + |DFLTS|) returns the project defaults path.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB obj_09_readConfiguration
!!filePath = !!evar(|PDMSUSER|) + |\EISConfiguration.xlsx|
if(!file.exists().not()) then
  var !projectCode PROJECT CODE
  !filePath = !!evar(!projectCode + |DFLTS|) + |\EISConfiguration.xlsx|
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using hardcoded paths instead of system variables
!filePath = 'C:\\project\\defaults\\config.xlsx'
pitfalls: PROJECT CODE requires being in a PDMS session context
DFLTS path depends on PDMS installation configuration
